On load, the app asks `/auth/me` who is signed in. `src/lib/auth.tsx` defines `getUser`, which calls `api.get('/auth/me')` and returns `response.data`. `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth` wraps it as `useUser()`, and `ProtectedRoute` (same file) wraps the `/app` subtree in `src/app/router.tsx`. If `useUser()` has no data, `ProtectedRoute` renders a `<Navigate>` to `/auth/login?redirectTo=<current path>`. The public routes (`/`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`) are not wrapped. `AuthLayout` in `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx` also calls `useUser()`, and once user data exists it navigates to `redirectTo` or the dashboard. The HTTP client is `src/lib/api-client.ts`, which sends credentials with every request (`withCredentials`, so the session cookie is included).

When any request gets a 401, the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` (lines 21-42) runs. It first shows an error toast with the server's message, then, if the status is 401, sets `window.location.href` to the login path. It also rejects the promise, so the calling query still fails. This is a full page load, not a router navigation, so the client state is reset.

There is a bug in the redirect. Line 34 creates `new URLSearchParams()` with no arguments, so `searchParams.get('redirectTo')` always returns null. The redirect target is therefore always `window.location.pathname`, and any query string on the current page is dropped. The fix is to read `window.location.search`. Because the interceptor also covers `/auth/me`, a signed-out visitor who opens a protected page can get both the toast and this full-page redirect.

Files involved: `src/lib/auth.tsx`, `src/lib/api-client.ts`, `src/app/router.tsx`, `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx`, `src/config/paths.ts`. I did not change any files.
